analysis: Integrated review of 5 units. Code change: new ServiceDrain.relaunchDrainedProvider (ServiceDrain+Recovery.swift) wraps the post-drain stop and relaunch in `defer { rearm(explicitConfig) }`. RestartCommand.swift (~37-40) and UpdateCommand.restartInstalledProvider (~163-166) now call it, so the crash-recovery watchdog is re-armed on relaunch failure as well as on success. Before, a failed relaunch left the provider down with recovery disabled. The drain-timeout fence in `prepare` is unchanged, so a timeout still leaves recovery disabled. Docs: changelog.d and docs/provider/cli-reference.md only describe this and the existing CLI, logout/unenroll (A-008, T-053), cache settings (T-041), the App Attest worker flag (TB-011), and fan helper paths (TB-010). Nothing there contradicts the threat model. Security view: net availability improvement (T-043, T-057). No new inputs, privileges, network surface or authority, and the same replaceable-binary watchdog (T-043) is re-enabled. Unverified items for deeper review, not findings, because rearmWatchdog's body and the watchdog/SelfUpdater state machine were not supplied: (1) in UpdateCommand the re-arm runs before the catch calls session.release()/cancelPendingCandidateAttempt (~167-170), so the watchdog may act on pending candidate state concurrently; (2) rearm also runs if stopDrainedProvider throws before the old process stopped, and on the LaunchAgentError.notInstalled path (RestartCommand ~41), so confirm it never arms a watchdog for an uninstalled provider; (3) rearm must not run after logout or an intentional stop, and must respect provider.auto_restart. No concrete regression is demonstrated. Coverage limits: some units had no diff hunks, so the exact doc changes are unverified.
